name: Non-aligned JPEG grid (NA-DJPG)
corpus: synthetic photo-like scenes generated from fixed seeds (forensic.validation.run.scene)

detection.task: Was the JPEG compressed before on a different 8x8 grid (cropped or shifted, then re-saved)?
detection.positives: 120 images saved at Q1 in {60, 75, 90}, cropped by a random non-zero (dx, dy), saved at Q2 = 90
detection.negatives: 240 images: saved once at {75, 90, 95}, or aligned double compressed (Q1, then 90)
detection.threshold_note: score = dip z-score / 10.0 for offsets off the final grid's axes, / 30.0 on them

known_failure_modes: Weak when the first save was at high quality (see tpr_by_first_quality).
Periodic scene content (brick, fences, text) can mimic a secondary grid.
Half-block offsets (4 px) are the most prone to false alarms.
Synthetic corpus: real-camera figures must be measured with --pristine or public datasets.
